notes.front: What is a Microsoft Entra tenant?
notes.back: An instance of Microsoft Entra ID holding one organisation’s users, groups, devices, app registrations and access policies.
notes.explanation: Each tenant acts as a security and administrative boundary, so it is the unit inside which an organisation controls access to its resources.
notes.example: Like a separate walled office building for one company: everyone and everything the company manages sits inside its walls.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Basic terminology”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a Microsoft Entra directory?
notes.back: The logical container inside a tenant that holds and organises identity objects such as users, groups, apps and devices.
notes.explanation: The course likens it to a database or catalogue of the tenant’s identities, and notes that people often use “directory” and “tenant” interchangeably.
notes.example: Like the staff and asset register kept inside that office building, as opposed to the building itself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Basic terminology”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a multitenant organization in Microsoft Entra terms?
notes.back: An organisation that runs more than one instance of Microsoft Entra ID, that is, more than one tenant.
notes.explanation: Separate subsidiaries, mergers and acquisitions, or different residency rules across regions can each lead an organisation to keep several tenants.
notes.example: Like a holding group whose three trading companies each keep their own building and register, yet still belong to one group.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Basic terminology”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the identity secure score in Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: A percentage showing how closely your configuration follows Microsoft’s recommended security practices for identity.
notes.explanation: It gives an objective measure of identity security posture, and its improvement actions are tailored to your own configuration.
notes.example: Like a fitness tracker’s weekly score, but measuring how well your sign-in and access settings follow the recommended routine.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Identity Secure Score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what is an external guest?
notes.back: A user who signs in with an external account or identity provider and whose user object has a UserType of Guest.
notes.explanation: Consultants, vendors and partners usually fall here; by default guests have fewer privileges than members.
notes.example: Like a visiting auditor who shows their own firm’s pass at reception and receives a visitor badge with limited access.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what is an external member?
notes.back: A user who authenticates with an account from another tenant but whose user object has a UserType of Member.
notes.explanation: It is common in organisations with several tenants, where people from a sister tenant need member-level access rather than guest access.
notes.example: Like an employee from a sister company in the same group who uses their own staff card but is given a full staff badge on arrival.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a workload identity?
notes.back: An identity given to a software workload, such as an app, service, script or container, so it can authenticate and reach other resources.
notes.explanation: The source notes the term is used inconsistently across the industry; broadly, it is what software needs to authenticate with a system.
notes.example: Like a staff card issued to a delivery robot rather than to a person, so doors know which machine is asking to come in.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Workload identities”, “What are workload identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A workload identity is an identity you assign to a software workload (such as an application, service, script, or container) to authenticate and access other services and resources. The terminology is inconsistent across the industry, but generally a workload identity is something you need for your software entity to authenticate with some system.

notes.front: What is a service principal?
notes.back: The local instance of an application in one specific tenant, defining what the app can do there and who can use it.
notes.explanation: An application object acts as a template, and a service principal is created from it in every tenant where the app is used.
notes.example: Like a franchise shop: the brand’s recipe book is global, but each local shop has its own licence setting what it may do in that town.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Workload identities”, “What are workload identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A service principal is the local representation, or application instance, of a global application object in a specific tenant. An application object is used as a template to create a service principal object in every tenant where the application is used.

notes.front: What is a managed identity?
notes.back: An identity assigned to an Azure compute resource, which can then be authorised to reach other resources.
notes.explanation: Examples of those downstream resources are a storage account or a database.
notes.example: Like a building that recognises the company van by its number plate, so the driver never needs to carry a key.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “What are managed identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Once a managed identity is assigned on the compute resource, it can be authorized, directly or indirectly, to access downstream dependency resources, such as a storage account, SQL database, Cosmos DB, and so on.

notes.front: What is a system-assigned managed identity?
notes.back: A managed identity enabled directly on one Azure resource, whose service principal lives and dies with that resource.
notes.explanation: Azure deletes the service principal automatically when the resource is deleted.
notes.example: Like a hotel key card printed for one room and one stay: it stops existing when the stay ends.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “Managed identity types” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: The service principal is tied to the lifecycle of that Azure resource. When the Azure resource is deleted, Azure automatically deletes the service principal for you.

notes.front: What is a user-assigned managed identity?
notes.back: A managed identity you create yourself and then assign to one or more Azure resources.
notes.explanation: Its service principal is managed separately from the resources that use it.
notes.example: Like a pool-car key kept at the front desk and lent to whichever team needs it.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “Managed identity types” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: You can create a user-assigned managed identity and assign it to one or more Azure Resources. When you enable a user-assigned managed identity: - A service principal of a special type is created in Microsoft Entra ID for the identity. The service principal is managed separately from the resources that use it.

notes.front: What is an agent identity in Microsoft Entra?
notes.back: A purpose-built identity for an artificial intelligence agent, provided by Microsoft Entra Agent ID and separate from traditional workload identities.
notes.explanation: Organisations use it to register agents, apply Conditional Access based on agent risk and govern each agent’s lifecycle with named owners.
notes.example: Like an ID card for a digital assistant that books travel for staff, with a named manager who answers for it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Agent identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a device identity in Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: An object in Microsoft Entra ID representing a device, similar to user, group or application objects.
notes.explanation: It gives administrators information they can use when deciding on access or configuration for that device.
notes.example: Like a serial-numbered asset tag on a laptop, which the security desk checks before letting it on the network.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is device identity in Microsoft Entra ID?”, “What is a device identity?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A device identity is an object in Microsoft Entra ID. This device object is similar to users, groups, or applications. A device identity gives administrators information they can use when making access or configuration decisions.

notes.front: What is a Microsoft Entra registered device?
notes.back: A device, typically personal, registered so its user can reach organisational resources in bring-your-own-device or mobile scenarios.
notes.explanation: Registration exists to support people who use their own phones, tablets or computers for work.
notes.example: Like signing your own bicycle into the office bike shed: it is still yours, but the building now knows it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a Microsoft Entra joined device?
notes.back: A device joined to Microsoft Entra ID through an organisational account, which is then used to sign in to it.
notes.explanation: Such devices are generally owned by the organisation rather than by the person using them.
notes.example: Like a company-issued phone that asks for your work login the first time you switch it on.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device?
notes.back: A device joined to both an on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID, signed in to with an organisational account.
notes.explanation: It lets organisations with an existing on-premises Active Directory gain Entra ID functionality for their devices.
notes.example: Like a staff pass that opens both the old headquarters and the new cloud-managed office.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a security group in Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: The most common group type, used to manage user and device access to shared resources.
notes.explanation: A group lets you grant access once to everyone with the same needs instead of assigning it person by person.
notes.example: Like a key ring labelled “finance”: anyone put on it can open the finance filing room.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a Microsoft 365 group?
notes.back: A group of users formed around collaboration needs, giving shared access to things like a mailbox, calendar, files and SharePoint sites.
notes.explanation: The course notes it is often also called a distribution group; its purpose is shared working space, not access policy.
notes.example: Like a project team’s shared office with its own letterbox, diary and filing cabinet.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is hybrid identity?
notes.back: A common user identity for authentication and authorisation to all resources, whether they are on-premises or in the cloud.
notes.explanation: It is Microsoft’s name for identity solutions that span on-premises and cloud-based capabilities.
notes.example: Like one staff card that works at both the old paper-records office and the new online portal.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID?”, “What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft’s identity solutions span on-premises and cloud-based capabilities. These solutions create a common user identity for authentication and authorization to all resources, regardless of location. We call this hybrid identity

notes.front: What is inter-directory provisioning?
notes.back: Provisioning an identity between two different directory service systems.
notes.explanation: In a hybrid environment the usual case is a user who already exists in Active Directory being provisioned into Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.example: Like copying a new starter from the head-office staff list onto the regional office’s list so they exist in both.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe hybrid identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In hybrid identity, what does synchronization do?
notes.back: It makes sure identity information for on-premises users and groups matches the cloud.
notes.explanation: It works alongside provisioning, which creates, updates and deletes objects according to conditions.
notes.example: Like a phone that keeps its contacts identical to your laptop’s, so a change on one appears on the other.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID?”, “What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Hybrid identity is accomplished through provisioning and synchronization. Provisioning is the process of creating an object based on certain conditions, keeping the object up to date and deleting the object when conditions are no longer met. Synchronization is responsible for making sure identity information for your on-premises users and groups is matching the cloud.

notes.front: What is the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM)?
notes.back: A standard specification for automating the exchange of user and group identity information between identity domains.
notes.explanation: The course describes it as becoming the de facto standard for provisioning.
notes.example: Like a standard postal address format that lets any courier deliver to any house without special instructions.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe hybrid identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kind of internal resources can Microsoft Entra ID give users access to? Give two examples.
notes.back: Apps on the corporate network and intranet; cloud apps the organisation developed itself.
notes.explanation: Entra ID covers resources the organisation runs itself as well as outside services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kind of external services can Microsoft Entra ID give users access to? Give two examples.
notes.back: Any two of: Microsoft 365; the Azure portal; SaaS applications the organisation uses.
notes.explanation: A single identity system then covers both the organisation’s own apps and outside services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A company already subscribes to Microsoft 365. Does it already have Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: Yes: every Microsoft 365, Azure or Dynamics online subscriber’s tenant is automatically a Microsoft Entra tenant.
notes.explanation: Management of access to integrated cloud apps can begin straight away.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Microsoft Entra?”, “Microsoft Entra ID” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: If you're a **Microsoft 365, Azure, or Dynamics CRM Online subscriber**, you're already using Microsoft Entra ID — every tenant is automatically a Microsoft Entra tenant. You can start managing access to your integrated cloud apps right away.

notes.front: Which two identifiers does every Microsoft Entra tenant have?
notes.back: A unique tenant ID and a domain name.
notes.explanation: These identifiers mark out the tenant as a distinct security and administrative boundary.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Basic terminology”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two reasons an organisation might have more than one Microsoft Entra tenant?
notes.back: Any two of: independent subsidiaries or business units; mergers or acquisitions; regions with different residency rules (among others).
notes.explanation: The course gives these as examples and leaves the list open.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Basic terminology”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which editions of Microsoft Entra ID include the identity secure score?
notes.back: All editions.
notes.explanation: No premium licence is needed to measure and track identity security posture.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe Microsoft Entra ID”, “Identity Secure Score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which product is the foundation of the Microsoft Entra family?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.explanation: It is the cloud identity and access management service that provides authentication, policy enforcement and protection for users, devices, apps and resources.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Microsoft Entra?”, “Microsoft Entra ID” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra ID is the foundational product of Microsoft Entra. It's a cloud-based identity and access management service that provides authentication, policy enforcement, and protection for users, devices, apps, and resources.

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra product lets remote users reach private apps and corporate networks without a VPN?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Private Access.
notes.explanation: It secures access to private apps and resources, including corporate networks and multicloud environments, from any device and network.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Microsoft Entra?”, “Microsoft Entra Private Access” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Private Access secures access to all private apps and resources, including corporate networks and multicloud environments. Remote users can connect to internal resources from any device and network without a VPN.

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra product issues verifiable credentials that users keep on their own devices?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Verified ID.
notes.explanation: It is a credential verification service built on open decentralised identity standards.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Microsoft Entra?”, “Microsoft Entra Verified ID” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Verified ID is a credential verification service based on open decentralized identity (DID) standards. Organizations can issue verifiable credentials — digital signatures that prove the validity of information — to users, who store the credentials on their personal devices and present them when needed.

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra product is the identity and access management solution for workload identities?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Workload ID.
notes.explanation: It secures applications, services and containers that need authentication and authorisation policies, using adaptive policies and custom security attributes.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Microsoft Entra?”, “Microsoft Entra Workload ID” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Workload ID is the identity and access management solution for workload identities — applications, services, and containers that require authentication and authorization policies. It lets organizations secure access to resources using adaptive policies and custom security attributes.

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra product extends Entra capabilities to artificial intelligence agents?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Agent ID.
notes.explanation: It gives assistive, autonomous and user-like agents purpose-built identities that can be authenticated, authorised, governed and protected.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is Microsoft Entra?”, “Microsoft Entra Agent ID” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Agent ID is an identity and security framework that extends Microsoft Entra capabilities to AI agents.

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what are identities assigned to people called?
notes.back: User identities.
notes.explanation: People are one of the three categories of thing that can be given an identity in Entra ID.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which category of Microsoft Entra identity covers phones, desktop computers and IoT devices?
notes.back: Device identities, assigned to physical devices.
notes.explanation: Physical hardware is a separate category from people and from software.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra ID, what are identities assigned to applications, virtual machines, services and containers called?
notes.back: Workload identities.
notes.explanation: Software-based objects form the third category, next to people and physical devices.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which two things characterise a user identity in Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: How the user authenticates (internal or external) and the user type property (member or guest).
notes.explanation: Combining the two gives four kinds of user: internal member, internal guest, external guest and external member.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: By default, guests in a Microsoft Entra tenant have {{c1::limited}} privileges compared with members.
notes.explanation: The user type property describes the user’s relationship to the host tenant, and access follows from it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of Microsoft Entra user authenticates through the organisation’s own Entra ID and has a UserType of Member?
notes.back: An internal member, typically an employee.
notes.explanation: Both properties point inwards: the account is in the host tenant and the user type is Member.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Why does the course call the internal guest a legacy scenario?
notes.back: Because it is now more common to use B2B collaboration, letting external users sign in with their own credentials.
notes.explanation: Internal guests are internal accounts created for outsiders such as distributors, with UserType set to Guest.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: External guests and external members are both which kind of user?
notes.back: B2B collaboration users, which fall under external identities in Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.explanation: Both authenticate outside the host tenant; they differ only in their user type.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra, workload identities are applications, service principals and what else?
notes.back: Managed identities.
notes.explanation: All three are identities for software, rather than for people or devices.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Workload identities”, “What are workload identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: In Microsoft Entra, workload identities are applications, service principals, and managed identities.

notes.front: What must happen before an application can delegate its identity and access functions to Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: It must be registered with Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.explanation: Registration enables the integration; a service principal is then created in each tenant where the app is used.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Applications and service principals”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two reasons workload identities are harder to secure than human identities?
notes.back: A workload may use several credentials that must be stored securely; it is hard to track when one is created or should be revoked.
notes.explanation: A person usually has one identity for many resources, whereas software may juggle many.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Workload identities”, “Need for securing workload identities” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Human users typically have a single identity used to access a broad range of resources. Unlike a human user, a software workload may deal with multiple credentials to access different resources and those credentials need to be stored securely. It’s also hard to track when a workload identity is created or when it should be revoked.

notes.front: What does a managed identity replace?
notes.back: Secrets such as access keys or passwords.
notes.explanation: The source adds that it can also replace certificates or other authentication for service-to-service dependencies.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “What are managed identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Managed identity replaces secrets such as access keys or passwords. In addition, managed identities can replace certificates or other forms of authentication for service-to-service dependencies.

notes.front: What are two benefits of managed identities for Azure resources?
notes.back: Any two of: no credentials to manage (they aren’t even accessible); authenticate to any Entra-authenticated resource; no extra cost.
notes.explanation: They can authenticate to your own applications too, not only to Azure services.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “What are managed identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: You don't need to manage credentials. Credentials aren’t even accessible to you. - You can use managed identities to authenticate to any resource that supports Microsoft Entra authentication, including your own applications. - Managed identities can be used at no extra cost.

notes.front: Which Azure resource can use a system-assigned managed identity to request tokens?
notes.back: Only the resource it was enabled on.
notes.explanation: The restriction is by design: the identity belongs to that one resource.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “Managed identity types” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: By design, only that Azure resource can use this identity to request tokens from Microsoft Entra ID.

notes.front: What happens to a user-assigned managed identity when the resources using it are deleted?
notes.back: Nothing: it has an independent life cycle and must be deleted explicitly.
notes.explanation: A system-assigned identity, by contrast, is deleted along with its parent resource.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “Differences between system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence:
Shared life cycle with the Azure resource that the managed identity is created with.
When the parent resource is deleted, the managed identity is deleted as well. | Independent life cycle.
Must be explicitly deleted.

notes.front: Which two kinds of scenario do agent identities support?
notes.back: Attended, where the agent acts on behalf of a user, and unattended, where it operates autonomously.
notes.explanation: Agent identities are specialised identities, distinct from traditional workload identities.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Agent identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are two things agent identities offer, according to Microsoft?
notes.back: Any two of: enforced human sponsorship; lifecycle governance from provisioning to deactivation; at-scale management across agent instances.
notes.explanation: Their management applies centralised security policies across all agent instances of a given type.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Workload identities”, “Agent identities for AI workloads” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Agent identities offer enforced human sponsorship, lifecycle governance from provisioning through deactivation, and at-scale management that apply centralized security policies across all agent instances of a given type.

notes.front: What are the three ways a device gets an identity in Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra registration, Microsoft Entra join and Microsoft Entra hybrid join.
notes.explanation: The overview gives exactly these three routes; the course calls the results registered, joined and hybrid joined devices.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is device identity in Microsoft Entra ID?”, “What is a device identity?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: There are three ways to get a device identity: - Microsoft Entra registration - Microsoft Entra join - Microsoft Entra hybrid join

notes.front: Device identities are a prerequisite for which two scenarios?
notes.back: Device-based Conditional Access policies, and mobile device management with Microsoft Intune.
notes.explanation: Without a device identity, neither of these scenarios can be set up.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is device identity in Microsoft Entra ID?”, “What is a device identity?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Device identities are a prerequisite for scenarios like device-based Conditional Access policies and Mobile Device Management with the Microsoft Intune family of products.

notes.front: How does Microsoft describe Microsoft Entra hybrid join relative to Microsoft Entra join?
notes.back: As an interim step on the road to Microsoft Entra join.
notes.explanation: All three device scenarios can still coexist in a single organisation.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is device identity in Microsoft Entra ID?”, “Modern device scenario” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra hybrid join is seen as an interim step on the road to Microsoft Entra join. All three scenarios can coexist in a single organization.

notes.front: Besides users, what can be members of a security group? Name two.
notes.back: Any two of: devices; other groups; service principals; agent identities.
notes.explanation: Microsoft 365 groups, by contrast, can hold only users.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Members of a Microsoft 365 group can only be {{c1::users}}, including users outside the organisation.
notes.explanation: A Microsoft 365 group exists for people who collaborate, not for devices or apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Through which two processes is hybrid identity accomplished?
notes.back: Provisioning and synchronization.
notes.explanation: Provisioning creates, updates and deletes objects according to conditions.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID?”, “What is hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra ID?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: Hybrid identity is accomplished through provisioning and synchronization. Provisioning is the process of creating an object based on certain conditions, keeping the object up to date and deleting the object when conditions are no longer met.

notes.front: Which tool does Microsoft recommend for synchronisation in a new hybrid identity deployment?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync.
notes.explanation: New identity and synchronisation features are being developed mainly on the Cloud Sync platform.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe hybrid identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is happening to Microsoft Entra Connect Sync?
notes.back: It is an earlier on-premises synchronisation tool that is being replaced by Cloud Sync.
notes.explanation: The course therefore treats Cloud Sync, not Connect Sync, as the path forward for new deployments.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe hybrid identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does an organisation need to deploy on-premises to use Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync?
notes.back: Only a lightweight cloud provisioning agent, in its on-premises or IaaS-hosted environment.
notes.explanation: The provisioning configuration itself is stored in Microsoft Entra ID and managed as part of the service.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe hybrid identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which specification does the Cloud Sync provisioning agent use to provision and deprovision users and groups?
notes.back: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM).
notes.explanation: SCIM automates exchanging user and group identity information between identity domains such as Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe hybrid identity”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra External ID scenario lets employees work with outside business partners?
notes.back: Collaborating with business guests, using B2B collaboration in a workforce tenant.
notes.explanation: Guests sign in with their own credentials while the organisation keeps control of its corporate data.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe external identities”, “Describe external identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra External ID scenario is for organisations publishing apps to consumers or business customers?
notes.back: Securing apps for consumers and business customers, using customer identity and access management.
notes.explanation: Customer identity and access management adds features such as self-service sign-up, customised sign-in and customer account management.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe external identities”, “Describe external identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How do business guests authenticate in B2B collaboration?
notes.back: With their home organisation or identity provider; the host organisation holds no credentials for them and checks their eligibility.
notes.explanation: The guest keeps using existing credentials, and the host only decides what they may access.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID”, “Collaborate with business guests” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: There are no credentials associated with business guests. Instead, they authenticate with their home organization or identity provider, and then your organization checks their eligibility for guest collaboration.

notes.front: Which feature does B2B direct connect currently enable?
notes.back: Teams Connect shared channels, for chat, calls, file sharing and app sharing with other organisations.
notes.explanation: B2B direct connect sets up two-way trust between Entra organisations, which the shared-channels feature relies on.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID”, “B2B direct connect” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: You can use B2B direct connect to create two-way trust relationships with other Microsoft Entra organizations to enable the Teams Connect shared channels feature. This feature allows users to seamlessly sign in to Teams shared channels for chat, calls, file sharing, and app sharing.

notes.front: An app runs on one virtual machine and needs to read from a storage account. The identity should disappear when that virtual machine is deleted. What should the team use?
notes.back: B: a system-assigned managed identity.
notes.choices:
A) A user-assigned managed identity
B) A system-assigned managed identity
C) An external guest account
D) A Microsoft 365 group
notes.choicesExplained: A lives on after the virtual machine is deleted until someone removes it. C is for human users from outside. D groups people for collaboration and is not an identity for software.
notes.explanation: Its life cycle is shared with its parent resource, so deleting the virtual machine deletes the identity too.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “Differences between system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence:
Shared life cycle with the Azure resource that the managed identity is created with.
When the parent resource is deleted, the managed identity is deleted as well.

notes.front: Twenty virtual machines are rebuilt often, but they must all keep the same access to one database. Which identity fits best?
notes.back: B: one user-assigned managed identity shared by all the virtual machines.
notes.choices:
A) A system-assigned managed identity on each virtual machine
B) One user-assigned managed identity shared by all the virtual machines
C) An agent identity
D) A password stored in each virtual machine’s configuration
notes.choicesExplained: A would be deleted and recreated with every rebuild. C is for artificial intelligence agents. D is the kind of stored secret managed identities replace.
notes.explanation: Microsoft lists workloads on several resources that share one identity, and resources recycled often with steady permissions, as its use cases.
notes.source: Microsoft, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”, “Differences between system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence:
Workloads that run on multiple resources and can share a single identity.
Workloads needing preauthorization to a secure resource, as part of a provisioning flow.
Workloads where resources are recycled frequently, but permissions should stay consistent.

notes.front: A build-and-deploy pipeline running in GitHub must deploy a web app to Azure App Service. Which kind of identity would a developer typically use for it?
notes.back: B: a service principal.
notes.choices:
A) A Microsoft Entra registered device
B) A service principal
C) An external member
D) A security group
notes.choicesExplained: A is for personal devices. C is a human user from another tenant. D grants access to members but is not itself the pipeline’s sign-in identity.
notes.explanation: Microsoft gives a pipeline deploying from GitHub to App Service as a typical use of a service principal.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Workload identities”, “What are workload identities?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: A service principal used by a developer to enable a CI/CD pipeline to deploy a web app from GitHub to Azure App Service.

notes.front: A nurse wants to read work email on her own mobile phone. How would that phone typically be set up in Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: A: as a Microsoft Entra registered device.
notes.choices:
A) As a Microsoft Entra registered device
B) As a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
C) As a Microsoft Entra joined device
D) As a user-assigned managed identity
notes.choicesExplained: B also needs on-premises Active Directory. C is for devices generally owned by the organisation and signed in to with a work account. D is for Azure resources, not phones.
notes.explanation: Registration is meant for bring-your-own-device and mobile scenarios where the device belongs to the user.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”

notes.front: A cloud-only start-up buys Windows 11 laptops for staff, who sign in with their work accounts. It has no on-premises Active Directory. How should the laptops be set up?
notes.back: A: as Microsoft Entra joined devices.
notes.choices:
A) As Microsoft Entra joined devices
B) As Microsoft Entra registered devices
C) As Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices
D) As external guests
notes.choicesExplained: B suits personal devices. C needs an on-premises Active Directory, which the start-up lacks. D is a user type, not a device state.
notes.explanation: Joined devices are generally owned by the organisation and are signed in to with an organisational account.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A bank’s desktops are already joined to its on-premises Active Directory. It wants them known to Microsoft Entra ID as well. Which device state fits?
notes.back: A: Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft Entra hybrid joined
B) Microsoft Entra joined
C) Not possible without removing Active Directory
D) Microsoft Entra registered
notes.choicesExplained: B joins the device to Entra ID alone. C is wrong because hybrid join exists for exactly this case. D is for personal devices.
notes.explanation: Hybrid joined devices are joined to both on-premises Active Directory and Entra ID, for organisations with an existing Active Directory.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A marketing team wants a shared mailbox, calendar and SharePoint site for a campaign. Which group type fits?
notes.back: A: a Microsoft 365 group.
notes.choices:
A) A Microsoft 365 group
B) A security group
C) A multitenant organization
D) A service principal
notes.choicesExplained: B manages access to shared resources and policies, not shared collaboration spaces. C describes an organisation with several tenants. D is an app’s identity.
notes.explanation: Microsoft 365 groups exist to group users by collaboration needs, with shared mailbox, calendar, files and sites.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An admin needs one group containing both users and their devices, to target with a Conditional Access policy. Which group type must it be?
notes.back: D: a security group.
notes.choices:
A) A Microsoft 365 group
B) A distribution list in a user’s mailbox
C) A Microsoft Entra directory
D) A security group
notes.choicesExplained: A cannot contain devices. B is not a Microsoft Entra group type in the course. C is the container for all objects in a tenant, not a group.
notes.explanation: Security groups can hold users, devices, other groups, service principals and agent identities; Microsoft 365 groups hold users only.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”

notes.front: A consultant from another company signs in to your tenant with her own firm’s account. Her user object has UserType Guest. What kind of user is she?

notes.choices:
A) An external guest
B) An internal member
C) An external member
D) An internal guest

notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”

notes.front: Two tenants belong to one large group. Staff from tenant X sign in to tenant Y with their X accounts, but need the same access as Y’s own staff. How are they set up in Y?
notes.back: B: as external members.
notes.choices:
A) As internal guests
B) As external members
C) As internal members
D) As external guests
notes.choicesExplained: A uses accounts created in Y and has only guest privileges. C would mean they authenticate with Y accounts. D has UserType Guest, so limited privileges.

notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “User”

notes.front: A council is starting a new hybrid identity project to keep on-premises Active Directory users matching Microsoft Entra ID. Which tool does the course point it to?
notes.back: C: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft Entra Domain Services
B) Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
C) Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync

notes.front: A retailer is launching a shopping app and wants customers to sign up with Google or Facebook accounts, kept apart from its staff directory. Which tenant configuration fits?
notes.back: B: an external tenant.
notes.choices:
A) A workforce tenant with B2B collaboration
B) An external tenant
C) A multitenant organization
D) B2B direct connect
notes.choicesExplained: A is for employees and business guests. C is an organisation with several instances of Entra ID. D is a trust between two Entra organisations for Teams shared channels.
notes.explanation: An external tenant configuration is exclusively for apps published to consumers or business customers, with its own directory of customer accounts.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID”, “What are workforce and external tenants?” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)

notes.evidence: An *external* tenant configuration is exclusively for apps that you want to publish to consumers or business customers. This distinct tenant follows the standard Microsoft Entra tenant model but is configured for consumer scenarios. It contains your app registrations and a directory of consumer or customer accounts.

notes.front: Two engineering firms, both using Microsoft Entra, want people to chat and share files in a Teams shared channel without adding each other as guests. What should they use?
notes.back: B: B2B direct connect, enabled by both organisations.
notes.choices:
A) B2B collaboration
B) B2B direct connect, enabled by both organisations
C) An external tenant
D) Internal guest accounts
notes.choicesExplained: A adds the partners as guest users in your directory. C is for consumer and business-customer apps. D means creating accounts for them in your own tenant, a legacy approach.
notes.explanation: B2B direct connect users authenticate at home and are not added as guests to the other workforce directory.
notes.source: Microsoft, “Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID”, “B2B direct connect” (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub)
notes.sourceLicence: B · MIT
notes.evidence: When two organizations mutually enable B2B direct connect, users authenticate in their home organization and receive a token from the resource organization for access. Unlike B2B collaboration, B2B direct connect users aren't added as guests to your workforce directory.

notes.front: An organisation deploys an artificial intelligence agent that files expense claims on its own overnight, and wants a named sponsor accountable for it. Which identity type is purpose-built for this?
notes.back: B: an agent identity.
notes.choices:
A) An external guest
B) An agent identity
C) A system-assigned managed identity
D) A Microsoft Entra registered device
notes.choicesExplained: A is a human user from outside. C is a workload identity tied to one Azure resource, without agent sponsorship. D represents a personal device.
notes.explanation: Agent identities are distinct from traditional workload identities and support unattended scenarios with owners and sponsors for accountability.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Agent identities”

notes.front: A container that runs a payroll calculation service needs its own identity in Microsoft Entra ID. Which category of identity is this?
notes.back: B: a workload identity.
notes.choices:
A) A user identity
B) A workload identity
C) A device identity
D) An external identity
notes.choicesExplained: A is for people. C is for physical hardware such as phones and computers. D describes users from outside the organisation.

notes.front: A staff member signs in once with Microsoft Entra ID. Which of these is an external service, in the course’s sense, that she can then reach?

A) An app on the corporate intranet
B) A cloud app her organisation built itself
C) The Azure portal
D) An app on the corporate network

notes.front: System-assigned versus user-assigned managed identity: which can be shared across Azure resources?
notes.back: Only user-assigned; a system-assigned identity is tied to a single resource.
notes.explanation: So several resources that need identical access can use one user-assigned identity between them.

notes.evidence:
Can’t be shared.
It can only be associated with a single Azure resource. | Can be shared.
The same user-assigned managed identity can be associated with more than one Azure resource.

notes.front: Microsoft Entra registered versus Microsoft Entra joined: who typically owns the device?
notes.back: Registered: usually the user (personal device). Joined: generally the organisation.
notes.explanation: Registration targets bring-your-own-device and mobile use; joining signs the device in with a work account.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Device”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Security group versus Microsoft 365 group: what is each for?
notes.back: Security group: managing user and device access to shared resources. Microsoft 365 group: grouping users for collaboration.
notes.explanation: This purpose shows in membership: security groups can hold devices and apps, Microsoft 365 groups only users.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe types of identities”, “Groups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Workforce tenant versus external tenant: whom does each contain?
notes.back: Workforce: employees, internal business apps and invited business guests. External: only apps published to consumers or business customers.
notes.explanation: Which configuration to choose depends on how the organisation intends to use the tenant.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn, “Describe external identities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: B2B collaboration versus B2B direct connect: which one adds the external user to your directory as a guest?
notes.back: B2B collaboration. B2B direct connect users stay in their home tenant and reach shared resources from there.
notes.explanation: Direct connect rests on mutual trust between two Entra organisations rather than on guest accounts.
